In 2020, Robin Sloan wrote about BoopSnoop , a messaging app he built for his family. Four people downloaded it. He considered this a resounding success. His point was simple: an app can be a home-cooked meal. You don't need scale. You don't need users. You cook for the people you love.

The app took him a week to build, half of it lost to code-signing purgatory. He wrote: "In a better world, I would have built this in a day, using some kind of modern, flexible HyperCard for iOS."

Six years later, the essay resurfaced on X when Thariq wrote that "personal software was a bit early in 2020 but in 2026, it really can be as personal as a home cooked meal, or a handwritten letter."

Lee Robinson wrote about the same shift . AI has made "personal computing" actually personal . He and his wife built a baby tracker because they didn't need "user profiles, badges, subscription tiers, or any other extra features."

I spent the past six months building way too much personalized software:

Our sleep consultant's plan arrived as a PDF full of conditional logic: wake windows, nap caps, what to do when a nap fails. Turning it into an app took a week of evenings. Now my wife, our nanny, and I share one live schedule that re-plans itself when a nap runs short.

My fitness app is built around my goals and connects data sources in a way no single app can. It knows my weekly run schedule, courtesy of the marathon app below, so it adjusts my daily calorie targets based on that morning's run distance and intensity. It tells me how many extra carbs and protein to eat before and after long runs, and reminds me to carb load the night before. It knows my smoothie recipe, eight ingredients I weigh out every morning, and sizes each portion to that day's training.

My running app skips the plan templates and derives everything from my Strava history and race results, including heart rate zones computed from races I ran instead of a formula involving my age.

Sloan's sovereignty point holds up too. "There will be no sudden redesign, no flood of ads, no pivot to chase a userbase inscrutable to us." My wife's favorite feature in the sleep app will be there as long as she wants it.

I'm been using the same stack for a couple years now and continue to love it. It lets me build fast and gives me full control over implementation details.

There are plenty of other great ways to do this, including less technical tools like Claude Artifacts , Replit , and Lovable that can get you a working app without touching a terminal.

The whole thing costs me about $160/mo: $100 for Claude Code Max, $10 in Anthropic API usage, $20 for Vercel, and $30 for Neon.

That's probably more than I'd pay for subscriptions to all these apps combined. But the bulk of the cost is my Claude subscription, which I'd keep regardless. Most of the Neon and API costs come from my slightly larger projects, nycjazz.guide and Claude Code Daily , not the personal apps. Before I upgraded from Claude Pro to Max it was under $100/mo.

Most of these services have generous free tiers, so if you're running one or two apps you could likely keep it to a $20/mo agentic coding subscription and ~$5-10/mo in model API usage.

The cost to build dropped off a cliff. The sleep app took a week of evenings. The fitness app took a weekend. The jazz quiz took a single evening after the kids went to bed. A year or two ago I wouldn't have considered building any of these: too slow to build, even harder to maintain. Imagination is now the limiting factor.

Maintenance is surprisingly easy. At least so far. Sloan's essay has a running gag in its yearly updates: "I have added one (1) feature, at my mother's request." In 2020 that made sense, because each change cost him a fight with Xcode. I've found fixing bugs, adding new features and dependency bumps to be easier than ever. 9/10 times a feedback screenshot shared with Claude gets the job done.

Aggregate data, add an LLM. The cost drop doesn't just mean more apps, it means apps can be far more personal. Most of mine follow the same shape: pull data from multiple sources, combine it in one place, and use an LLM to generate insights from the full picture. My fitness app combines nutrition, sleep, weight, and training data that lives in four separate apps, then uses that context to make recommendations none of them could alone. I think this pattern will spread to professional tools too.

Ephemeral is fine. We used the sleep app for about four months. Our son sleeps through the night now, so we retired it. If the app had taken me months to build, that might sting. Because it took a week, I'm just glad it worked when we needed it.

AI floods big markets and unlocks small ones. Yes, AI produces endless derivative apps . But the same tools also let me build apps for my household that no company would bother making. Beyond my household, I built nycjazz.guide for NYC jazz fans and claudecodedaily.com for Claude Code developers, audiences too small for a business but worth serving.

Good APIs matter more than ever. I switched from Cronometer to FatSecret because FatSecret had a better API. My fitness app pulls from Strava, Oura, Withings, and FatSecret, and the quality of each integration depends on how well the API is designed. As more people build personal software, users will expect their apps to have APIs and MCPs worth connecting to.

Building is the point, not just the result. These apps solve real problems for me and the people I care about: how well our son sleeps, my health, my running. That part is rewarding. But I also spend my evenings after the kids are asleep building these instead of watching Netflix or scrolling X. It's my preferred source of entertainment now.

It's not just fun. It's addictive. Agentic coding has slot machine mechanics. You're one prompt away from the next feature or unlock, so you keep pulling. The irony isn't lost on me: I've ruined more than a few nights of sleep building apps to improve my health.

chineseContent:
2020 年，Robin Sloan 写了一篇关于 BoopSnoop 的文章，这是他为家人开发的一款消息应用程序。有四个人下载了。他认为这是一次巨大的成功。他的观点很简单：应用程序可以成为一顿家常饭菜。你不需要规模。你不需要用户。你为你爱的人做饭。

这个应用程序花了他一周的时间来构建，其中一半的时间都输给了代码签名炼狱。他写道：“在一个更好的世界里，我会在一天内使用某种现代、灵活的 iOS HyperCard 构建出这个应用程序。”

六年后，这篇文章在 X 上重新出现，塔里克写道：“个人软件在 2020 年出现还为时过早，但到 2026 年，它真的可以像一顿家常菜或一封手写信一样个性化。”

Lee Robinson 写了同样的转变。人工智能使“个人计算”真正变得个人化。他和他的妻子建立了一个婴儿追踪器，因为他们不需要“用户个人资料、徽章、订阅级别或任何其他额外功能”。

在过去的六个月里，我构建了太多的个性化软件：

我们的睡眠顾问的计划以 PDF 形式提供，其中充满了条件逻辑：唤醒窗口、午睡上限、午睡失败时该怎么办。把它变成一个应用程序花了一周的时间。现在，我的妻子、我们的保姆和我共享一个实时时间表，当午睡时间不够时，它会自动重新计划。

我的健身应用程序是围绕我的目标构建的，并以任何单个应用程序都无法做到的方式连接数据源。它知道我每周的跑步计划（由下面的马拉松应用程序提供），因此它会根据当天早上的跑步距离和强度调整我的每日卡路里目标。它告诉我长跑前后需要摄入多少额外的碳水化合物和蛋白质，并提醒我前一天晚上摄入碳水化合物。它知道我的冰沙配方、我每天早上称量的八种成分，并根据当天的训练调整每份的大小。

我的跑步应用程序会跳过计划模板，并从我的 Strava 历史记录和比赛结果中获取所有内容，包括根据我跑步的比赛计算得出的心率区，而不是涉及我年龄的公式。

斯隆的主权观点也成立。 “不会有突然的重新设计，不会有大量的广告，也不会以追逐我们难以理解的用户群为中心。”我妻子在睡眠应用程序中最喜欢的功能只要她想要，就会一直存在。

我已经使用同一个堆栈好几年了，并且仍然喜欢它。它让我可以快速构建并让我完全控制实现细节。

还有很多其他很好的方法可以做到这一点，包括技术含量较低的工具，如 Claude Artifacts 、 Replit 和 Lovable ，它们可以让您在不接触终端的情况下获得一个可以运行的应用程序。

整个过程花费我大约 160 美元/月：Claude Code Max 100 美元，Anthropic API 使用费 10 美元，Vercel 20 美元，Neon 30 美元。

这可能比我订阅所有这些应用程序所支付的费用总和还多。但大部分费用是我的克劳德订阅费，无论如何我都会保留它。大多数 Neon 和 API 成本来自我稍大的项目 nycjazz.guide 和 Claude Code Daily，而不是个人应用程序。在我从 Claude Pro 升级到 Max 之前，每月价格不到 100 美元。

这些服务中的大多数都有慷慨的免费套餐，因此，如果您正在运行一两个应用程序，您可能会将其保持在 20 美元/月的代理编码订阅和约 5-10 美元/月的模型 API 使用量。

建造成本急剧下降。睡眠应用程序花了一周的晚上时间。健身应用程序花了一个周末。孩子们睡觉后，爵士乐测验花了一个晚上的时间。一两年前，我不会考虑构建任何这些：构建速度太慢，维护起来更困难。想象力现在已成为限制因素。

维护非常简单。至少到目前为止。斯隆的文章在每年的更新中都有一个不断出现的笑话：“应我母亲的要求，我添加了一 (1) 个功能。”在 2020 年，这是有道理的，因为每一次改变都让他与 Xcode 发生了争执。我发现修复错误、添加新功能和依赖项冲突比以往任何时候都更容易。 9/10 倍，与 Claude 分享的反馈屏幕截图可以完成工作。

汇总数据，添加法学硕士。成本下降不仅意味着更多的应用程序，还意味着应用程序可以更加个性化。我的大部分工作都遵循相同的模式：从多个来源提取数据，将其组合到一个地方，然后使用法学硕士从全局中生成见解。我的健身应用程序结合了营养、睡眠、体重和训练数据，这些数据存在于四个独立的应用程序中，然后使用该上下文提出任何一个单独的应用程序都无法提供的建议。我认为这种模式也会传播到专业工具中。

短暂的就好。我们使用睡眠应用程序大约四个月。我们的儿子现在睡整夜了，所以我们把它退休了。如果这个应用程序花了我几个月的时间来构建，那可能会很痛苦。因为花了一周的时间，我很高兴它在我们需要的时候发挥了作用。

人工智能涌入大市场并解锁小市场。是的，AI会产生无穷无尽的衍生应用程序。但同样的工具也让我可以为我的家庭构建没有公司愿意制作的应用程序。除了我的家庭之外，我还为纽约爵士乐迷建立了 nycjazz.guide，为 Claude Code 开发人员建立了 claudecodedaily.com，这些受众对于企业来说太小，但值得服务。

良好的 API 比以往任何时候都更重要。我从 Cronometer 切换到 FatSecret，因为 FatSecret 有更好的 API。我的健身应用程序来自 Strava、Oura、Withings 和 FatSecret，每个集成的质量取决于 API 的设计程度。随着越来越多的人构建个人软件，用户将期望他们的应用程序具有值得连接的 API 和 MCP。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
